Generate an Artificial Longitudinal Dataset with Mixed-type Outcomes

generate_longitudinal_mixed_type_data.Rd

Five different longitudinal outcomes are sampled according to the model described by Vávra et al. (2024). Column i is the unit id, j is the number of observation for ith unit. Numeric ynum, count ypoi, binary ybin, ordinal yord and categorical ycat outcomes are sampled according to predictors pred_... which are constructed from the intercept, time covariate x, categorical covariate f and the random effects b_.... The definition of the predictor can be adjusted.

Usage

generate_longitudinal_mixed_type_data(n, n_i = 4, G = 2, timepar = "parallel", 
  catpar = "no", catsubjfix = TRUE, xin1 = 1, Sigma, 
  Kord = 5, Kcat = 4, kspec_bi_cat = FALSE)

Arguments

n

number of sample units.

n_i

number of observations per unit.

G

number of clusters, only G=2 and G=3 are predefined.

timepar

a string declaring what is the parametrization of time covariate x. One of no, parallel, cross, spline, mix.

catpar

a string declaring what is the parametrization of binary covariate f. One of no, fixed, group.

catsubjfix

a logical value; should the values of categorical covariate be fixed for the same unit or alternate among observations?

xin1

1/xin1 is the width of observational window for one unit, so xin1 declares how many times does the observational period of one unit fit into the overall data gathering period.

Sigma

the covariance matrix for the random intercepts (of dimension 5, one for each outcome). Can be a list of covariance matrices, in such a case the model assumes group-specific covariance matrix.

Kord

number of categories for ordinal outcome.

Kcat

number of categories for categorical outcome (only up to 4 categories).

kspec_bi_cat

a logical value; should the random effects be specific to each level of categorical outcome? If so, the dimension of Sigma should be larger.

Details

The function generate_longitudinal_mixed_type_data is limited in the number of clusters G since it is quite laborious to define all the true values of model parameters (e.g. effects \(\beta\)).

Time covariate x is sampled so that observations for one unit are close to each other. First, half-length of the observational window xmid = 1/(2xin1) is defined. Then, values for a unit are sampled by uniform distribution on [-xmid, xmid] and randomly shifted by multiples of xmid. Time covariate is limited to interval [0, 1].

The spline parametrization (library("splines")) of the time covariate is of degree = 2 and has knots = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)

Binary covariate f is sampled with probability 0.5 either once per unit (catsubjfix = TRUE) or repeatedly for each observation (catsubjfix = FALSE).

The group allocation indicator g is sampled uniformly on {1, ..., G} for each unit.

Then the linear predictors for each observation and outcome are created according to selected parametrization of time covariate x (timepar) and parametrization of binary covariate f (catpar). The intercepts are always group-specific which ensures at least some difference among clusters.

Choices for timepar:

no

covariate x does not modify the predictor,

parallel

clusters have the same linear trend in time x but different intercepts,

cross

clusters have different linear trends in time x (one is increasing, another decreasing),

spline

each cluster has a different randomly generated spline parametrization,

mix

outcomes have different selection of all of the above (currently, numeric is spline, count is cross, binary is parallel, ordinal is spline, categorical is cross).

Choices for catpar:

no

covariate f does not modify the predictor,

fixed

clusters have the same effect of f,

group

clusters have different effects of f.

Numerical outcome is sampled from normal distribution with group-specific standard deviations (from 0.5 to 1.0).

Count outcome is sampled from Poisson distribution with rate made by exp() of the predictor.

Binary outcome (0 or 1) is sampled with probability computed by plogis.

Ordinal outcome (ordered factor) is sampled by probabilities computed by sequential differences of plogis applied to shifted predictor.

Categorical outcome (unordered factor) is sampled by probabilities computed by softmax function from several predictors specific for each category; softmax(x) = exp(x) / sum(exp(x)) where x is Kcat-dimensional. By default, predictor for the first category is set to 0 for identifiability purposes.

Value

A list containing:

data

a data frame with covariates, random effects, predictors and sampled outcomes,

sd_num

a vector of true values of standard deviations for numeric outcome depending on the total number of clusters G,

beta_num

a list of true values (named vector) of \(\beta\) parameters for numeric outcome for each cluster,

beta_poi

a list of true values (named vector) of \(\beta\) parameters for count outcome for each cluster,

beta_bin

a list of true values (named vector) of \(\beta\) parameters for binary outcome for each cluster,

beta_ord

a list of true values (named vector) of \(\beta\) parameters for ordinal outcome for each cluster,

c_ord

a list of true values of intercepts specific to each level of the ordinal outcome for each cluster,

beta_cat

a list of true values (matrix with named columns) of \(\beta\) parameters for categorical outcome for each cluster.

References

Vávra, J., Komárek, A., Grün, B., Malsiner-Walli, G. Clusterwise multivariate regression of mixed-type panel data. Stat Comput 34, 46 (2024). https://doi.org/10.1007/s11222-023-10304-5

Author

Implemented by Jan Vávra for performing a simulation study in Vávra et al. (2024).

Examples

n <- 100      
n_i <- 4       
G <- 2         
timepar <- "mix" 
catpar <- "no"  
catsubjfix <- TRUE 
xin1 <- 1        
Kord <- 5        
Kcat <- 4        
kspec_bi_cat <- FALSE
corr <- matrix(c(1, -0.5, -0.5, -0.4, -0.4,
                 -0.5, 1, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5,
                 -0.5, 0.3, 1, 0.2, 0.3,
                 -0.4, 0.4, 0.2, 1, 0.1,
                 -0.4, 0.5, 0.3, 0.1, 1), byrow = TRUE, ncol = 5)
sdSigmas <- c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5)
Sigma <- diag(sdSigmas) %*% corr %*% diag(sdSigmas)

set.seed(31415)
ldata <- generate_longitudinal_mixed_type_data(n = n, n_i = n_i,
                     G = G, timepar = timepar,
                     catpar = catpar, catsubjfix = catsubjfix,
                     xin1 = xin1, Sigma = Sigma,
                     Kord = Kord, Kcat = Kcat, kspec_bi_cat = kspec_bi_cat)
data <- ldata$data
